Djibouti City was founded by the French in 1888 on a coral headland on the south shore of the Gulf of Tadjoura, and became the capital of French Somaliland in 1896.

Its deep harbour faced the strait at the mouth of the Red Sea. The governor Léonce Lagarde chose it as the sea end of a railway to Ethiopia, and when the line was built the town grew into the main port for Ethiopian trade.

Today about three in five of the country's people live in the city. Its ports, the new terminals at Doraleh and the foreign military bases around it make up most of the national economy of Djibouti.
sum: Djibouti City was founded by the French in 1888 on a coral headland on the south shore of the Gulf of Tadjoura, and became the capital of French Somaliland in 1896.
